pairs.why: A keeps the real card's stiff flat sheets with straight edges and tighter corners, while B turns the stack into soft, wavy, rolled cloth with blobby corners.
A has the real card's boxy body with planar faces and thin straps, while B is puffier and its straps are thicker.
A's body is a chunky box with flat panels, a plate top and thin jointed legs, while B is a swollen pillow-shaped body with fat wheels.
A has the real card's squat, tall-bodied box, a thick loop handle and a deep, tilted lid, while B's body is flat and wide with a shallow lid and a thin handle.
B's big bass drum overlaps the toms in a compact mass like the real kit, while A's pieces are spread apart and look thinner; the difference is small.
A has a thick slab top with a heavy edge, a squat pedestal on a wide base and thick stools, matching the real proportions, while B has a thin tabletop on a tall skinny post.
A has a chunky, compact coil with one loop, close to the real cards' bulk and silhouette, while B splits into two thin separate rings with a dangling tail.
A has a short, compact barrel with a thin curved yoke like the real lamp, while B has a long tube and a rectangular, angular bracket.
